concepts.learning_objective: Describe the structure of a typical anther and the wall layers of a microsporangium with their functions.
Explain how pollen mother cells form microspore tetrads by meiosis and work out the ploidy of the products.
Describe the two-layered wall and the two- or three-celled contents of a mature pollen grain.

topics.title: The pistil, ovule and embryo sac

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the parts of a typical angiosperm ovule such as funicle, hilum, integuments, micropyle, chalaza and nucellus.
Explain megasporogenesis and monosporic development of the embryo sac, including the ploidy of the cells involved.
Describe the 7-celled, 8-nucleate organisation of the mature embryo sac formed by free-nuclear mitosis.
Distinguish autogamy, geitonogamy and xenogamy, and chasmogamous from cleistogamous flowers.
Relate the features of wind- and water-pollinated flowers to the way their pollen is carried.
Explain how animal-pollinated flowers attract and reward pollinators, including plant-pollinator mutualism.

topics.title: Outbreeding devices, pollen-pistil interaction and artificial hybridisation

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the devices that discourage self-pollination, including self-incompatibility, monoecy and dioecy.
Describe pollen recognition by the pistil and the path of the pollen tube to the synergid.
Explain emasculation and bagging and their order in a crop-improvement cross.
Identify the nuclei that take part in syngamy and in triple fusion inside the embryo sac.
Explain why fertilisation in angiosperms is called double fertilisation and work out the ploidy of its products.
Explain free-nuclear and cellular endosperm development and why endosperm forms before the embryo.
Compare the parts of dicotyledonous and monocotyledonous (grass) embryos.
Distinguish albuminous from non-albuminous seeds and identify perisperm and seed coats.
Explain the development of true, false and parthenocarpic fruits from floral parts.
Evaluate the role of dehydration, dormancy and viability of seeds in survival and agriculture.
Explain apomixis as asexual seed formation and its importance for hybrid seed production.
Explain how nucellar cells give rise to multiple embryos in a seed and the genetic nature of such embryos.
